lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- That Number Is Wrong
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 10 -- That Number Is Wrong

listenings.text: Thank you for flagging it, and before I say anything about the figure, could you confirm which version of the file you are looking at? The one from the fourteenth, or the one we reissued on the seventeenth? Right. Then two things. You are right that the description on that line was unclear, and I will change it in every report from now on. On the amount, though, I stand by it: the four thousand is a warehouse invoice that arrived after your export was taken, and it is backed up by the invoice itself, which I am attaching now. So neither number was wrong. They were taken on different dates. We will reconcile both versions line by line and come back to you before the end of the day.

Quick one before you all go. I have just come off the call with the client. He said his file and ours did not match on the warehouse line, a discrepancy of about four thousand. He asked whether we could resend the breakdown, and he wanted to know where the four thousand came from. I told him it was an invoice that landed after his export, and that we would send it across today. I conceded one thing: he said the description on the line was unclear, and he was right, so we are changing that wording everywhere. What I need from you: cross-check both versions against the invoices and come back to me before the end of the day. Not tomorrow morning. Today.

paras: Fabia, thanks for the report, which we have now been through with the finance team. Most of it lines up with what we have here. There is one item I would like to understand better before we sign it off.

On the warehouse line, your figure and ours differ by roughly four thousand. I am not saying your number is wrong. I am saying the two files do not agree, and I cannot approve a figure I cannot explain to my own board.

Two requests, then. Could you resend the breakdown for that line, and could you tell me where the four thousand comes from? If it is an invoice we have not seen, that would explain it, and I would rather know that today than argue about it next quarter.
One smaller point while I have you. The description on that line reads as if it covers the whole quarter, and I do not think it does. That is what sent us looking in the first place.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: when two numbers that should match do not
to make two sets of numbers agree, line by line
a formal question about one specific item
to accept the other side is right on one point
to check one source against another
to report a figure as bigger than it really is

items.situation: "Your warehouse figure is wrong." Report it to your team.
"Can you resend the breakdown?" Report it.
"Where does the four thousand come from?" Report it.
"We will not approve the report this week." Report it.
"We have already checked it against our invoices." Report it.
Now tell the team what you conceded, and what you did not.
